strategy.summary: Reproduce the empty-interval overlaps defect in pandas by building the buggy commit from source (Cython extension required because overlaps is implemented in pandas/_libs/interval.pyx) and running the two PR test files filtered to the new test_overlaps_empty tests. The scalar test asserts False for Interval(0,1,'both') against empty intervals closed left/right/neither, which the buggy revision returns True for, so it fails there and passes on the fixed revision. No version or dependency constraint is documented, so the strategy picks a recent NumPy and Python 3.11 or later and states that choice.

pinned_because: NumPy: no documented constraint and no era table entry, so the unpinned latest release compatible with the chosen Python is used; this is a choice, not an evidenced requirement
python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython: unbounded, no pin applied; versions are chosen only to allow the build and test run

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/scalar/interval/test_overlaps.py::TestOverlaps::test_overlaps_empty (parametrized over empty_closed in left/right/neither and offset 0/1/2), plus pandas/tests/arrays/interval/test_overlaps.py::TestOverlaps::test_overlaps_empty (the IntervalArray/IntervalIndex variant, with closed from the closed fixture)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 4bcadf56f045, test_overlaps_empty fails because Interval(start,start+2*shift,other_closed).overlaps(empty) or the reverse returns True for an empty interval with left==right and closed not 'both', so the assert not ... fails. On the fixed revision (the PR#67945 change), all selected test_overlaps_empty cases pass because empty intervals never overlap. test_overlaps_point is not part of the transition and should pass on both revisions.
risks: The defect lives in compiled Cython code (pandas/_libs/interval.pyx). A non-editable install or a Python-only rebuild will not pick up the fix, so the editable meson build command must be used so the extension is recompiled on import.

No platform or sanitiser dependence is evidenced; the behaviour is pure boolean logic on integer endpoints, so it should reproduce on any common Linux or macOS x86_64 or arm64 build. Nothing in the evidence shows it needs a specific architecture.

The arrays test file's test_overlaps_empty uses the fixtures closed, constructor and start_shift; their availability in that test class's conftest was not confirmed by the evidence. If the closed fixture is missing, the arrays test will error rather than fail for the defect, and only the scalar test would show the transition.
The arrays test diff is truncated, so the full expected values for the non-empty-container branch are not visible; the transition is driven by the empty-element assertions, not those.
Interval(0,0,closed='both') is a point, not empty; test_overlaps_point guards this and is not part of the transition.

PR date and buggy-revision Python version were not stated; if a very new NumPy breaks the old buggy commit's build, pin NumPy to a version contemporaneous with the commit, but the evidence does not supply that version.

oracle.reference_source: PR#67945 test diff and the stated empty-interval rule in the docstring and whatsnew entry
oracle.why: Results are boolean, so the assertion is exact equality with False; no tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 4bcadf56f045, test_overlaps_empty asserts that a non-empty closed interval does not overlap an empty interval. The buggy overlaps returns True when the empty interval's closed side makes the boundary point 0 look shared, so the assertion 'assert not result' fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, overlaps returns False for every empty interval with left==right and closed not 'both', so all selected test_overlaps_empty cases pass.
